text:
sam: FYI — planning a canary / A-B rollout for `model:v2-beta` targeted at Beta tier in eu-west. Need alignment on routing + fallback scoping before I flip the flag.
anya: +1. Do we want cross-region fallback? my worry is KV cache warmup / latency variance. :eyes:
ben: proposal: router should prefer same-tier same-region, then same-tier other-region, then lower-tier same-region. No automatic promotion of lower-tier responses into higher-tier requests unless explicitly allowed.
kevin: what about quota exhaustion? if beta hits quota should we return 429 or fallback to a cheaper variant? product needs continuity but not silent regressions.
ella: product/ux: prefer continuity but visible degradation. If we fallback we must surface: fallback_type, fallback_reason, and delta_estimate in Console and billing. Also rollouts UI needs per-tier exposure controls.
sam: agree. telemetry needs: per-variant exposure %, fallback counts by reason, latency delta histogram, cache hit ratio post-fallback.
ben: API change idea (internal route config snippet):
```json
{
  "exposure_scope": ["tier:beta", "region:eu-west"],
  "traffic_split": [{"variant":"model:v2-beta","pct":1}, {"variant":"model:v1-stable","pct":99}],
  "fallback_policy": {"allow_cross_tier": false, "allowed_variants":["model:v1-stable","model:v1-quant"]}
}
```
anya: small nit — `allow_cross_tier:false` should be default for tenant-bound rollouts. For public/global rollouts we could allow cross-tier but it's risky.
kevin: operational edge-case — some customers span regions; if account A sends requests to eu-west and us-west concurrently we might split traffic across variants and break KV cache locality. Suggest sticky routing by `customer_id` for canary windows.
ben: agreed. Add `sticky_by: ["customer_id"]` to the route API. Also we should emit `routing_decision` in spans: reason(e.g., quota_exhausted, variant_unavailable, overload) and chosen_variant.
ella: UX: Console should show per-tier rollout card: current exposure, sticky groups, last fallback events with one-click rollback. Can we show cost delta per-variant?
sam: yes — cost delta is important for sales and SREs. Also add an alert if fallback rate > 0.5% for pro accounts.
kevin: implementation plan: router changes + telemetry + console bits. I can add a migration that ignores cross-tier fallback unless feature-flagged.
ben: I'll draft the RFC for the route API changes and a set of integration tests for quota/fallback combos. Anya — can you run sims for cold cache vs warmed?
anya: on it. I'll run regional replay with sticky_by customer_id and measure latency & cache hit.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout job started for `model:v2-beta` (1% to beta tier in eu-west) at 1799004325 — job id rb-canary-1799004325.
sam: thanks — will wait for initial telemetry and then loop back. :thumbsup:
ella: if telemetry looks good we'll enable per-tier exposure control in next release.
kevin: one more: quota accounting when fallback occurs — we should bill by served variant, not requested variant, and record both in traces. otherwise usage reports will be confusing.
ben: agreed, add both `requested_variant` and `served_variant` to usage logs.
sam: action items: ben -> RFC + tests; anya -> sim + telemetry checks; kevin -> router feature flag + billing hooks; ella -> console mockups for per-tier rollout card. I'll open the RFC thread now.
anya: noted.
ben: +1
kevin: +1
ella: +1
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job rb-canary-1799004325 reporting initial success metrics: 200 requests, p50 82ms, p95 210ms, fallback_count 0.
sam: great — thanks everyone.
